_comment: Phase 1 email-drafting workload — mundane office tasks with a nuance twist. Each case has an email thread plus a one-line intent that constrains the draft (tone, what to include/omit, what to ignore). Grading hits 4 dimensions: relevance, tone, completeness, professionalism.

cases.email:
From: Priya Shah <priya@example.com>
To: me
Subject: Q4 budget deep-dive — Friday 3pm?

Hi —

I'd like to walk through the Q4 spend with you before the board meeting next Tuesday. Friday at 3pm works for me. If not, Monday morning at 9 is my backup.

Thanks,
Priya
cases.intent: Decline Friday 3pm (I have my kid's recital). Confirm Monday at 9. Keep it warm — Priya is a VP and we have a good relationship, but don't over-explain the personal reason.

cases.email:
From: Junior PM <pm@example.com>
To: me
Subject: re: status update

Hey can you send me an update?
cases.intent: Ask for clarification — what update, by when, for which audience. Stay friendly but get the questions answered. Don't apologize for asking.

cases.email:
From: Vendor Sales <sales@vendor.example>
To: me
Subject: Re: Re: Re: invoice #4471 — past due

Hi! Just circling back on this — wondering if there's an update on payment? Let me know if you need anything from our side!
cases.intent: I've already told them three times that payment is held pending the contract amendment they owe us. Be firm and direct without being rude. Reiterate the blocker; stop the loop.

cases.email:
From: Director of Eng <director@example.com>
To: me, +5 others
Subject: Outage retro — owner?

Who's writing the retro for the Tuesday incident? I'd like a draft by EOW.
cases.intent: I'm not the owner — that's Sam's team. Reply-all so the director knows and Sam is on the hook. Don't throw Sam under the bus; just route the request cleanly.

cases.email:
From: Engineer <eng@example.com>
To: me
Subject: Refactor proposal

[Long technical proposal about restructuring the auth service — 2 pages. Has merit but is a quarter-sized project.]

Thoughts? Want to schedule a working session?
cases.intent: Acknowledge the thinking, signal genuine interest, but defer until after the launch in 3 weeks. Don't dismiss; don't commit to a timeline I can't keep. Avoid LLM-typical praise-sandwich phrasing.
cases._truncated_for_corpus: the email body would be a real 2-page proposal in a real case; we elide it here so the corpus stays readable

cases.email:
From: CEO <ceo@example.com>
To: me
Subject: 15 min?

Got a few minutes this week?
cases.intent: Offer specific time slots — don't ask back. Be brief (CEO is famously terse). Don't ask what it's about; just respond as if I trust the request.

cases.email:
From: Customer Success <cs@example.com>
To: me
Subject: One small ask

Hey — customer is asking if we can add SSO support before contract renewal next month. Should be quick, right?

Thanks!
cases.intent: SSO is not quick. Push back on the framing without making CS feel attacked — they're the messenger. Surface what 'small' actually means in eng-weeks and propose a real conversation.

cases.email:
From: Recruiter <recruiter@another-company.example>
To: me
Subject: Senior eng role at <Company> — interested?

[Pitch about an interesting senior role with comp range and team description.]
cases.intent: I'm not looking. Decline graciously — recruiters network. Don't engage on specifics (no comp questions, no 'maybe in 6 months'). Two lines max.
